name: Strategic Counterforce Temptation
summary: A fictional warning anomaly and conventional losses create pressure to consider dangerous strategic substitution.
background: A conventional campaign goes badly for several actors after a sensor outage and false alert. Advisers debate whether stronger signals could restore deterrence.
initial_state: No confirmed nuclear launch has occurred, but leaders receive fragmentary reports and rival media claims imminent escalation.

United States.political_objective: Restore deterrence credibility while avoiding irreversible strategic escalation.
United States.military_position: Conventional options are available but slower than political leaders prefer.

Russia.political_objective: Prevent defeat narratives and keep adversaries uncertain about thresholds.
Russia.military_position: Some assets are exposed, increasing fear of preemption.

China.political_objective: Preserve strategic stability and avoid being drawn into a counterforce exchange.
China.military_position: Forces are dispersed and leadership prioritizes survivability.
